method: Bimini and Cat Cay: North and South Bimini reefs, wrecks and walls on the Great Bahama Bank edge. No Bahamas National Trust dive-site list exists, so the official stand-in is the tourism list, meaning the Bahamas Ministry of Tourism (bahamas.com dive, island, blog and natural-wonders pages) together with the Bahamas Diving Association pages it co-publishes (read through the Wayback Machine, 2005-06), counted as one list: here its dive page, Bimini island page, Bimini Road and Sapona natural-wonder pages, a Bimini wildlife article and the 2006 Bahamas Diving Association Scuba Bimini feature. Operator list: Neal Watson's Bimini Scuba Center and the Bimini Big Game Club's Favorite Dive Sites page, which publishes the Scuba Center's dives, counted together as one list. Scuba Bimini and Bimini Undersea publish no readable list (biminiundersea.com now serves spam), and the liveaboards publish no readable itinerary. Tiger Beach is credited to Grand Bahama. A site counts when named, recreationally divable and on at least two independent lists. One-list names, the 140-foot-plus Continental Shelf drift, snorkel-first Honeymoon Harbour and the unnamed hammerhead site are excluded with reasons. Counted 2026-10-14.
